newsitem.title: USA: CanAmera Foods says to cut Canada canola crush.
newsitem.headline: CanAmera Foods says to cut Canada canola crush.

text.p: CanAmera Foods is to cut its canola crush in Canada by "20 percent or more" in late November due to poor crush margins, a spokesman said.
He said the company was the largest integrated crusher-refiner in Canada and accounted for about 52 percent of the Canadian industry.
The cutback would reduce its Canadian crush by about 25,000 tonnes a month, he added.

The news followed an earlier announcement by Cargill Ltd that it would temporarily cease crushing operations at its plant in Clavet, Saskatchewan until "market conditions turn around." Cargill Ltd is the Canadian unit of Cargill Inc.
The CanAmera spokesman said profit margins on canola were currently "non-existent."
CanAmera is 50 percent owned by Central Soya, which is itself owned by private French company Eridania Begain-Say.
The Canadian company is also 50 percent owned by a partnership of Manitoba Pool Elevators and the Saskatchewan Wheat Pool.
"The dominating factor is that there is a protective and punitive duty on oil imports into Japan and Mexico, two of the prime buyers of Canadian canola," the CanAmera spokesman said.
He said the duty in Japan was about C$200 a ton and in Mexico C$45.00 a ton, allowing their crushers to raise bids for seed without worrying about competition from imported oil.
"They can just keep bidding the price up until they destroy the Canadian margin," he said.
A reduction in the size of Canada's canola crop and an increase in Canada's crushing capacity were also contributory factors to margin weakness, the spokesman added.
